title: Ship-derived tech explains the setting's uneven tech level, and why the Watcher reads comms trivially
summary: Frame technology, and anything else built on the same substrate including the party's phones, came from the mitflits' crashed ships (dug out, copied, and leaked outwards) rather than being organically developed, which is why 1950s-level ordinary society coexists with giant mechs, and why the Watcher, native to that same alien substrate, can read anything running on it without 'hacking' it in any conventional sense. (Corrected 2026-09-24, LEDGER #33: this said the technology was 'excavated from the Gap'. The Gap is an event after this adventure, not a dig; the description and sub-questions were corrected to match on 2026-09-25.)
description:
Confirms and extends a thread already floated as a 'strong implication, not confirmed as a rule yet' in design/campaign-arc.md's Setting tone section: the coexistence of tall sailing ships and giant excavated mechs in the same harbor isn't an inconsistency to smooth over, it's the point. Frame technology was never organically developed by this society — it came out of the mitflits' crashed ships (Gen 1 copied from what was seen there, Gen 2 built from the real thing), is narrow and scarce, and is only partially understood even by the Directorate that controls it. That's exactly why it's institutionally gatekept and why only specifically-trained pilots can touch it at all. Ordinary civilian life never had to invent the underlying physics, so it never diffused outward the way genuinely home-grown technology would — society advanced everywhere except the narrow, jealously-guarded excavated band. Now confirmed rather than left as an implication.

New this pass: the player phones (and plausibly other Directorate infrastructure) run on the same ship-derived substrate as the Gen 2 Frames — not a deliberate Directorate design choice, but because ship technology is apparently the only way to build something with a phone's capability at all in a society that's otherwise stuck at roughly a 1950s tech level. That's *why* the phones exist as advanced objects in a retro-industrial world: the same worldbuilding move as the Frames themselves, applied to a second piece of hardware.

The payoff, and the reason this idea exists: the Watcher doesn't 'hack' the phones in any conventional sense. Hacking implies breaking into a system that's otherwise closed to you. The Watcher is native to the substrate the phones (and the Gen 2 Frames) are built from — reading comms traffic on ship technology isn't an intrusion for it, any more than a fish hacks the water it swims in. This is deliberately a different category of act from a Claimant rolling Recall Knowledge against a PC in combat (see watcher-recall-knowledge-on-party and watcher-reads-all-comms): that's earned, imperfect, and dice-rolled, because predicting live, contested combat behavior is a genuinely hard modeling problem even for something this vast. Reading stored or transmitted text through hardware it's already native to is not remotely the same problem, and shouldn't need a roll, a DC, or a security mechanic the party could ever meaningfully harden against. There's no patch for being the wall.
sourceContext: User message, 2026-09-02: 'we need a good reason for tech to be all over the place with some things being in a 1950s like historical state but also things like giant Mechs. the watcher runs on the alien tech so decoding the player Comms based on alien tech is trivial.' Given directly as the answer to (and confirmation of) the uneven-tech implication already flagged in design/campaign-arc.md.
openSubQuestions: Does this extend to all Directorate electronics/infrastructure (sensors, terminals, the intranet) or specifically comms/phones? 2026-09-24: the rewritten quarantine/ideas/story/dossier-observer.md says the phones and the Directorate's own electronics both run on the substrate the ships were built from. That is Claude's writing, not an Ingram decision.

ANSWERED IN PART 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #32, from Ingram's Casebook N4: 'But the technology still leaks outwards.'): the leak -- the phones, and anything else too advanced for the era -- is ship technology leaking outwards from the Kortos site, the generation ship opened by First Impact. Still open: whether the Directorate's own electronics come from that same leak or from the search ship under Kurose. (Corrected 2026-09-24, LEDGER #34: this called the search ship under Kurose 'Gen 2's source', here and in the question as first asked, below. That was Claude's inference; Ingram's own words put Gen 2's technology at the First Impact crash site (#20) and in 'the original ship' (#34), so Gen 2 comes from the generation ship too.) As first asked: Which ship's technology the phones and the Directorate's electronics derive from: the Kortos specimen (Gen 1's source, itself of unclear origin -- open-questions.json#bisected-specimen-origin; withdrawn by LEDGER #32, there is no specimen), the search ship under Kurose, or both. Open since LEDGER #31 made two ships (2026-09-24).

Does ordinary civilian technology ever incorporate a slow trickle-down of ship-technology components over the campaign, or does the gate stay hard for the whole campaign? 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #32; Ingram, N4): the gate has never been fully hard. Ship technology has already leaked out of the Kortos site despite the Directorate. Whether it keeps trickling into civilian life over the campaign is still open.

Whether other factions (the cicada organization) have their own partial access to ship technology, or the Directorate's excavation is genuinely singular. 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #32): the leak means others can have some. Claude's proposal, veto freely: William Charles Baldwin, among the first to loot the opened Kortos site, arms criminal gangs with weapons built from leaked ship technology by essentially enslaved mitflits (GM-only; quarantine/ideas/story/bible/characters/william-charles-baldwin.md).
Whether this connects at all to Golarion's existing magic-and-fey layer (the campaign's other confirmed genre-blend element) or stays a separate, parallel explanation for a separate phenomenon.
resolution: RE-GROUNDED 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31). Two things moved under this idea since it was captured. (1) 'THE GAP' IS NOW A FUTURE EVENT, not a past span or a dig site (open-questions.json#the-gap-is-future, 2026-09-20), so the technology came from the ships, not from a Gap dig. The id keeps the old word so links don't break; the title was corrected on 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #33), and the description and sub-questions on 2026-09-25. (2) THE SUBSTRATE IS NOW CONCRETE: it is the technology of the mitflits' two crashed ships. Gen 1 Frames were written up here as reverse-engineered from a bisected specimen at Kortos (withdrawn by LEDGER #32, below: there is no specimen), and Gen 2 Frames are built from the generation ship's technology (LEDGER #20, #34; corrected 2026-09-24: this said the search ship whose hull lies under Kurose, citing LEDGER #31 item 1, which was Claude's inference; see below). Which ship the phones derive from was open; LEDGER #32 answers it (below). THE PAYOFF IS SHARPER: the Watcher is the generation ship's own navigation and sensor system (LEDGER #31 item 3). If the phones derive from either ship, they run on technology its own makers built, and reading them is not hacking, exactly as this entry always said. The central claim stands: ordinary society stayed roughly 1950s because the one advanced band was dug up rather than invented, and is jealously gatekept. FURTHER, 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #32; Ingram, Casebook N4). THE LEAK HAS A SOURCE: First Impact opened up the generation ship's inner layers at Kortos. Scientists and magic-users descended on it, adventurers came for valuables, and the organisations around Kortos banded together to guard it -- the Directorate's birth -- partly to stop the uncovered technology disrupting the world. "But the technology still leaks outwards." So the setting's out-of-era technology (the phones, and anything else too advanced for the era) is ship technology leaking outwards from the Kortos site, despite the Directorate. GEN 1 is Golarion technology only, informed by looking at that ship: mechanical, with no living core. GEN 2 is different in kind: Anabala building mechs from actual mitflit technology (item 7). Gen 2 is built from the generation ship's technology: the original ship, the First Impact crash site at Kortos, which the Directorate holds and keeps restricted from the rest of Golarion (LEDGER #20, #34). (Corrected 2026-09-24, LEDGER #34: this said the search ship under Kurose. That was Claude's inference; Ingram's own words put Gen 2's technology at the First Impact crash site (#20) and in 'the original ship' (#34).) THE PAYOFF IS LITERAL NOW: the Watcher is the generation ship's navigation and sensor system, and the leaked technology comes from that same ship, so the phones run on technology from the Watcher's own ship, and reading them is not hacking. The central claim stands, adjusted: ordinary society stayed roughly 1950s because the advanced band was dug up rather than invented and is jealously gatekept, and it leaks anyway. FURTHER, 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #33; Ingram, Casebook N24): the Gap is an event after the adventure, perhaps a result of it, perhaps the only way to undo Second Impact, so nothing in play is 'Gap-derived'. The title and summary now say ship-derived, and since 2026-09-25 so do the description and sub-questions; the id keeps the old word so links don't break. FURTHER, 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #34; Ingram, Casebook D13 and N25). ONE SHIP BEHIND MOST OF THE BAND: with Gen 2's source corrected above to the generation ship, the leak, Gen 1's inspiration and Gen 2's material all come from the one ship the Watcher was part of. Only the Directorate's own electronics are still open between it and the search ship (openSubQuestions). THE GATE, IN INGRAM'S WORDS: the Directorate keeps the original ship's technology 'highly restricted to the rest of Golarion to stop it having a destabilising effect on the world', which is this idea's 'jealously gatekept'. ANABALA'S ACCESS: she works with the Directorate, and has her own ultimate objective, using mitflit technology to get a way home for her people; building Gen 2 for the Directorate was her price for access to the original ship's technology. THE GEN 2 CORE: biomechanical mitflit technology, robotic parts that are living flesh melded with technology, not a living mitflit; these mechs aren't usable by just anyone.
